findings.location: AD-PSI-7 typed document-symbol decision (lines 294-301), test strategy item 0 (line 494), and PR-EO-002 closure claim (line 654)
findings.affected_requirement: The approved decision and August architecture require exactly one current same-path JDT-LS top-level Type to validate the profile-owned semantic owner; PR-EO-002 requires the real adapter boundary to prove that authority without synthesizing Type evidence.
findings.evidence: The corrected parser plan treats a SymbolInformation item as top-level when containerName is absent/null/empty and ignores nonempty-container items. The official LSP 3.18 document-symbol contract states that SymbolInformation[] is a flat list and that neither its location range nor containerName may be used to infer hierarchy; containerName is UI information only. Therefore this rule cannot prove top-level ownership. The same plan accepts DocumentSymbol items without requiring their protocol-mandatory selectionRange or proving it is contained by range. Current JdtLsAnalysisAdapter has no response-shape/top-level provenance, so PreparedJavaRangeSource cannot repair this distinction downstream. PR-EO-002 is not closed by raw tests that encode a protocol-invalid hierarchy inference.
findings.correction_outcome: Revise AD-PSI-7, research, contract and tests so semantic-owner authority comes only from hierarchy that the protocol can actually prove. The smallest option is to require a homogeneous DocumentSymbol[] response for semantic-owner binding, validate mandatory name/kind/range/selectionRange plus selectionRange containment, and trust only root items as top-level; SymbolInformation[] may remain usable for unrelated generic behavior only if it cannot acquire semantic-owner authority. Alternatively carry an explicit protocol-grounded hierarchy provenance, but do not infer it from SymbolInformation.containerName. Preserve definition/references/implementation behavior and all existing bounds/fail-closed ordering.

findings.location: AD-PSI-7 Prepared Pass 1 projection (lines 333-337), Project Structure and Ownership (lines 479-484), test strategy items 12-13 (lines 507-508), and PR-EO-001 closure claim (line 653)
findings.affected_requirement: The approved proposal requires the same semantic symbol through the Prepared Pass 1 Worker packet and Source Anchor, while PR-EO-001 requires complete server-only SymbolName propagation and repeated v1/v2 validation without provider exposure.
findings.evidence: The plan now correctly adds SymbolName to PreparedPass1WorkerPacket and PreparedPass1FileCodeUnitAssignment, and owns the claimed source, dispatcher and executor. However the production call chain hydrates a packet and then Vulgata.Web/Data/PreparedPass1JobRunner.CreateDispatchRequest reconstructs a new PreparedPass1FileCodeUnitAssignment positionally from that packet. This is the only packet-to-assignment bridge and currently has no SymbolName expression. The plan never names PreparedPass1JobRunner, its Web ownership says only PreparedScanPairBuilder changes, and the implementation intent limits Web work to the matched builder. Adding a required assignment field without changing and testing this bridge cannot compile or cannot preserve the semantic symbol; changing it would exceed the enumerated ownership. PR-EO-001 is therefore only partially closed.
findings.correction_outcome: Add PreparedPass1JobRunner.CreateDispatchRequest to the narrow Web ownership and test matrix solely to forward the required server-owned SymbolName from the hydrated packet into the assignment. Require an exact semantic and path-valued round-trip test across hydrated packet -> job runner dispatch request -> dispatcher packet, plus a mutation/omission failure proving no executor/provider call. Update implementation intent and task-author instructions accordingly; do not change scheduling, retry, job state, provider request, prompts, tools or public composition.

summary: REVISE. The corrected plan materially improves the design and closes much of attempt-01: it now owns actual LSP kind parsing, preserves unrelated navigation, adds server-only SymbolName to the Prepared Pass 1 assignment/packet, reconstructs v1/v2 identity at claimed-source/dispatcher/executor checkpoints, excludes SymbolName from provider-visible requests, preserves path-valued v1 bytes and semantic-only v2, aligns Source Anchors with the unchanged Story 12.4 lookup, fails before publication/provider use, keeps external analysis outside transactions, and adds no migration/public input/CGC/Story 12.4 mutation. Two High plan defects remain. PR-EO-002 is not genuinely closed because the proposed SymbolInformation.containerName rule infers hierarchy where the official LSP 3.18 contract explicitly forbids that inference, and its DocumentSymbol acceptance omits mandatory selectionRange validation. PR-EO-001 is not genuinely closed because the production PreparedPass1JobRunner packet-to-assignment bridge is absent from ownership and tests. Both corrections stay within the approved exact-owner scope and belong to the plan; tasks and implementation remain unauthorized. The AGENTS.md Scan planned-change gate remains mandatory after a fresh independent ACCEPT because the design materially changes matched-profile JDT-LS document-symbol handling, File Code Unit identity, and internal Prepared Pass 1 propagation. The unrelated user-owned .env.example and immutable attempt-01 verdict were excluded from authored ownership; reviewed-path git diff --check passed.
